explanation: Ben should obtain permission from the client to perform scans before engaging in any other activities. Failure to do so may violate the law and/or anger the client.

stem: Katherine coordinates the remediation of security vulnerabilities in her organization and is attempting to work with a system engineer on the patching of a server to correct a moderate impact vulnerability. The engineer is refusing to patch the server because of the potential interruption to a critical business process that runs on the server. What would be the most reasonable course of action for Katherine to take?
explanation: The fact that the server runs a critical business process should increase the importance of the patch, rather than deferring it indefinitely. Katherine should work with the engineer to schedule the patch to occur during a regular maintenance window. It is reasonable to wait until that scheduled window because of the relatively low impact of the vulnerability.

choices.label: A
choices.body: Schedule the patching to occur during a regular maintenance cycle.

choices.label: B
choices.body: Exempt the server from patching because of the critical business impact.

choices.label: C
choices.body: Demand that the server be patched immediately to correct the vulnerability.

choices.label: D
choices.body: Inform the engineer that if he does not apply the patch within a week that Katherine will file a complaint with his manager.

stem: Grace ran a vulnerability scan and detected an urgent vulnerability in a public-facing web server. This vulnerability is easily exploitable and could result in the complete compromise of the server. Grace wants to follow best practices regarding change control while also mitigating this threat as quickly as possible. What would be Grace’s best course of action?
explanation: In this situation, Grace is facing a true emergency. Her web server has a critical vulnerability that is exposed to the outside world and may be easily exploited. Grace should correct the issue immediately, informing all relevant stakeholders of the actions that she is taking. She can then follow up by documenting the change as an emergency action in her organization’s change management process. All of the other approaches in this question introduce an unacceptable delay.

choices.label: A
choices.body: Initiate a high-priority change through her organization’s change management process and wait for the change to be approved.

choices.label: B
choices.body: Implement a fix immediately and document the change after the fact.

choices.label: C
choices.body: Schedule a change for the next quarterly patch cycle.

choices.label: D
choices.body: Initiate a standard change through her organization’s change management process.

stem: Joe discovered a critical vulnerability in his organization’s database server and received permission from his supervisor to implement an emergency change after the close of business. He has 8 hours before the planned change window. In addition to planning the technical aspects of the change, what else should Joe do to prepare for the change?
explanation: Joe has time to conduct some communication and change management before making the change. Even though this change is urgent, Joe should take advantage of that time to communicate with stakeholders, conduct a risk assessment, and initiate change management processes. These tasks will likely be abbreviated forms of what Joe would do if he had time to plan a change normally, but he should make every effort to complete them.

choices.label: A
choices.body: Ensure that all stakeholders are informed of the planned outage.

choices.label: B
choices.body: Document the change in his organization’s change management system.

choices.label: C
choices.body: Identify any potential risks associated with the change.

stem: Sally discovered during a vulnerability scan that a system she manages has a high-priority vulnerability that requires a patch. The system is behind a firewall and there is no imminent threat, but Sally wants to get the situation resolved as quickly as possible. What would be her best course of action?
explanation: In this situation, Sally recognizes that there is no imminent threat, so it is not necessary to follow an emergency change process that would allow her to implement the change before conducting any change management. That said, the change should be made without waiting up to 3 months for a scheduled patch cycle. Therefore, Sally’s best option is to initiate a high-priority change through her organization’s change management process.

choices.label: A
choices.body: Initiate a high-priority change through her organization’s change management process.

choices.label: B
choices.body: Implement a fix immediately and then document the change after the fact.

choices.label: C
choices.body: Implement a fix immediately and then inform her supervisor of her action and the rationale.

choices.label: D
choices.body: Schedule a change for the next quarterly patch cycle.

stem: Gene runs a vulnerability scan of his organization’s datacenter and produces a summary report to share with his management team. The report includes the chart shown here. When Gene’s manager reads the report, she points out that the report is burying important details because it is highlighting too many unimportant issues. What should Gene do to resolve this issue?
explanation: Gene’s best option is to alter the sensitivity level of the scan so that it excludes low-importance vulnerabilities. The fact that his manager is telling him that many of the details are unimportant is his cue that the report contains superfluous information. Although he could edit the chart manually, he should instead alter the scan settings so that he does not need to make those manual edits each time he runs the report.

choices.label: A
choices.body: Tell his manager that all vulnerabilities are important and should appear on the report.

choices.label: B
choices.body: Create a revised version of the chart using Microsoft Excel.

choices.label: C
choices.body: Modify the sensitivity level of the scan.

choices.label: D
choices.body: Stop sharing reports with the management team.

stem: Glenda routinely runs vulnerability scans of servers in her organization. She is having difficulty with one system administrator who refuses to correct vulnerabilities on a server used as a jump box by other IT staff. The server has had dozens of vulnerabilities for weeks and would require downtime to repair. One morning, her scan reports that all of the vulnerabilities suddenly disappeared overnight, while other systems in the same scan are reporting issues. She checks the service status dashboard, and the service appears to be running properly with no outages reported in the past week. What is the most likely cause of this result?
explanation: Although any of these reasons are possible, the most likely cause of this result is that the system administrator blocked the scanner with a host firewall rule. It is unlikely that the administrator completed the lengthy, time-consuming work overnight and without causing a service disruption. If the server were down, other IT staff would have reported the issue. If the scan did not run, Glenda would not see any entries in the scanner’s logs.

choices.label: A
choices.body: The system administrator corrected the vulnerabilities.

choices.label: C
choices.body: The system administrator blocked the scanner.

stem: Tom is planning a series of vulnerability scans and wants to ensure that the organization is meeting its customer commitments with respect to the scans’ performance impact. What two documents should Tom consult to find these obligations?
explanation: Tom should consult service level agreements (SLAs) and memorandums of understanding (MOUs). These documents should contain all commitments made to customers related to performance. Disaster recovery plans (DRPs) and business impact assessments (BIAs) should not contain this type of information.

stem: Zhang Wei is evaluating the success of his vulnerability management program and would like to include some metrics. Which one of the following would be the least useful metric?
explanation: Zhang Wei should likely focus his efforts on high-priority vulnerabilities, as vulnerability scanners will report results for almost any system scanned. The time to resolve critical vulnerabilities, the number of open critical vulnerabilities over time, and the number of systems containing critical vulnerabilities are all useful metrics. The total number of reported vulnerabilities is less useful because it does not include any severity information.

choices.label: B
choices.body: Number of open critical vulnerabilities over time

choices.label: D
choices.body: Number of systems containing critical vulnerabilities

stem: Donna is working with a system engineer who wants to remediate vulnerabilities in a server that he manages. Of the report templates shown here, which would be most useful to the engineer?
explanation: The Technical Report will contain detailed information on a specific host and is designed for an engineer seeking to remediate the system. The PCI Technical Report would focus on credit card compliance issues, and there is no indication that this server is used for credit card processing. The Qualys Top 20 Report and Executive Report would contain summary information more appropriate for a management audience and cover an entire network, rather than provide detailed information on a single system.

stem: Abdul received the vulnerability report shown here for a server in his organization. The server runs a legacy application that cannot easily be updated. What risks does this vulnerability present?
explanation: The use of FTP is not considered a good security practice. Unless tunneled through a secure protocol, FTP is unencrypted, allowing an attacker to eavesdrop on communications and steal credentials that may be transmitted over FTP links. Additionally, this vulnerability indicates that an attacker can gain access to the server without even providing valid credentials.

choices.label: A
choices.body: Unauthorized access to files stored on the server

stem: William is preparing a legal agreement for his organization to purchase services from a vendor. He would like to document the requirements for system availability, including the vendor’s allowable downtime for patching. What type of agreement should William use to incorporate this requirement?
explanation: Service level agreements (SLAs) specify the technical parameters of a vendor relationship and should include coverage of service availability as well as remedies for failure to meet the agreed-on targets. Memorandums of understanding (MOUs) are less formal documents that outline the relationship between two organizations. Business partnership agreements (BPAs) typically cover business, rather than technical, issues and would not normally include availability commitments. Business impact analysis (BIA) documents are risk assessments and are not legal agreements.

stem: Raul is replacing his organization’s existing vulnerability scanner with a new product that will fulfill that functionality moving forward. As Raul begins to build the policy, he notices some conflicts in the scanning settings between different documents. Which one of the following document sources should Raul give the highest priority when resolving these conflicts?
explanation: Of the documents listed, only corporate policy is binding on Raul, and he should ensure that his new system’s configuration complies with those requirements. The other sources may provide valuable information to inform Raul’s work, but compliance with them is not mandatory.

choices.label: D
choices.body: Configuration settings from the prior system

stem: Pietro is responsible for distributing vulnerability scan reports to system engineers who will remediate the vulnerabilities. What would be the most effective and secure way for Pietro to distribute the reports?
explanation: There is no reasonable justification for Pietro reviewing the reports prior to providing them to the administrators responsible for the systems. In the interests of transparency and efficiency, he should configure the scans to run automatically and send automated notifications to administrators as soon as they are generated. This approach allows immediate remediation. There is nothing preventing Pietro from performing a review of the scan results, but he should not filter them before providing them to the responsible engineers.

choices.label: A
choices.body: Pietro should configure the reports to generate automatically and provide immediate, automated notification to administrators of the results.

choices.label: B
choices.body: Pietro should run the reports manually and send automated notifications after he reviews them for security purposes.

choices.label: C
choices.body: Pietro should run the reports on an automated basis and then manually notify administrators of the results after he reviews them.

choices.label: D
choices.body: Pietro should run the reports manually and then manually notify administrators of the results after he reviews them.

stem: Nitesh would like to identify any systems on his network that are not registered with his asset management system because he is concerned that they might not be remediated to his organization’s current security configuration baseline. He looks at the reporting console of his vulnerability scanner and sees the options shown here. Which of the following report types would be his best likely starting point?
explanation: The Unknown Device Report will focus on systems detected during the scan that are not registered with the organization’s asset management system. The High Severity Report will provide a summary of critical security issues across all systems. The Technical Report will likely contain too much detail and may not call out unknown systems. The Patch Report will indicate systems and applications that are missing patches but not necessarily identify unknown devices.

stem: Nabil is the vulnerability manager for his organization and is responsible for tracking vulnerability remediation. There is a critical vulnerability in a network device that Nabil has handed off to the device’s administrator, but it has not been resolved after repeated reminders to the engineer. What should Nabil do next?
explanation: The scenario does not indicate that Nabil has any operational or managerial control over the device or the administrator, so his next step should be to escalate the issue to an appropriate manager for resolution. Nabil should not threaten the engineer because there is no indication that he has the authority to do so. Nabil cannot correct the vulnerability himself because he should not have administrative access to network devices as a vulnerability manager. He should not mark the vulnerability as an exception because there is no indication that it was accepted through a formal exception process.

choices.label: A
choices.body: Threaten the engineer with disciplinary action.

choices.label: C
choices.body: Mark the vulnerability as an exception.

choices.label: D
choices.body: Escalate the issue to the network administrator’s manager.

stem: Maria discovered an operating system vulnerability on a system on her network. After tracing the IP address, she discovered that the vulnerability is on a proprietary search appliance installed on her network. She consulted with the responsible engineer who informed her that he has no access to the underlying operating system. What is the best course of action for Maria?
explanation: Maria should contact the vendor to determine whether a patch is available for the appliance. She should not attempt to modify the appliance herself, as this may cause operational issues. Maria has no evidence to indicate that this is a false positive report, and there is no reason to wait 30 days to see whether the problem resolves itself.

choices.label: A
choices.body: Contact the vendor to obtain a patch.

choices.label: B
choices.body: Try to gain access to the underlying operating system and install the patch.

choices.label: C
choices.body: Mark the vulnerability as a false positive.

choices.label: D
choices.body: Wait 30 days and rerun the scan to see whether the vendor corrected the vulnerability.

stem: Thomas is working with an application team on the remediation of a critical SQL injection vulnerability in a public-facing service. The team is concerned that deploying the fix will require several hours of downtime and will block customer transactions from completing. What is the most reasonable course of action for Thomas to suggest?
explanation: This is a critical vulnerability in a public-facing service and should be patched urgently. However, it is reasonable to schedule an emergency maintenance for the evening and inform customers of the outage several hours in advance to avoid business process interruption. Therefore, Thomas should immediately begin monitoring affected systems for signs of compromise and work with the team to schedule maintenance for as soon as possible.

choices.label: A
choices.body: Wait until the next scheduled maintenance window.

choices.label: B
choices.body: Demand that the vulnerability be remediated immediately.

choices.label: C
choices.body: Schedule an emergency maintenance for an off-peak time later in the day.

choices.label: D
choices.body: Convene a working group to assess the situation.

stem: Thomas discovers a vulnerability in a web application that is part of a proprietary system developed by a third-party vendor, and he does not have access to the source code. Which one of the following actions can he take to mitigate the vulnerability without involving the vendor?
explanation: Thomas can deploy a web application firewall to block attempts to exploit the vulnerability. Applying a patch or updating the source code may also resolve the issue, but Thomas cannot do this himself because he does not have access to the source code. Dynamic testing identifies vulnerabilities but does not correct them.

stem: Walt is designing his organization’s vulnerability management program and is working to identify potential inhibitors to vulnerability remediation. He has heard concern from functional leaders that remediating vulnerabilities will impact the ability of a new system to fulfill user requests. Which one of the following inhibitors does not apply to this situation?
explanation: Walt finds himself in a very common situation, with business leaders worried about the impact of vulnerability remediation on their activities. The business leaders are concerned about business process interruption and degrading functionality. This could be best resolved with a robust organizational governance process. The system in question is newly deployed, so it is not an example of a legacy system.

stem: The company that Brian works for processes credit cards and is required to be compliant with PCI DSS. If Brian’s company experiences a breach of card data, what type of disclosure will they be required to provide?
explanation: Organizations that process credit cards work with acquiring banks to handle their card processing, rather than directly with the card providers. Notification to the bank is part of this type of response effort. Requiring notification of law enforcement is unlikely, and the card provider listing specifies only two of the major card vendors, none of which are specified in the question.

stem: As Ava prepares her organization’s security practices and policies, she wants to address as many threat vectors as she can using an awareness program. Which of the following threats can be most effectively dealt with via awareness?
explanation: Improper usage, which results from violations of an organization’s acceptable use policies by authorized users, can be reduced by implementing a strong awareness program. This will help ensure users know what they are permitted to do and what is prohibited. Attrition attacks focus on brute-force methods of attacking services. Impersonation attacks include spoofing, on-path/intermediary-in-the-middle attacks, and similar threats. Finally, web-based attacks focus on websites or web applications. Awareness may help with some specific web-based attacks like fake login sites, but many others would not be limited by Ava’s awareness efforts.

stem: Laura wants to ensure that her team can communicate during an incident. Which of the following should the team prepare to be ready for an incident?
explanation: A distinct messaging system that can work if enterprise services are unavailable due to an incident can be a critical factor for IR teams. Whether it’s a phone tree, a collaboration system that also allows distinct logins that are not part of enterprise authentication, or another solution, IR teams often need a system that is separate during wide-ranging incidents.

choices.label: A
choices.body: A second, enterprise authenticated messaging system

choices.label: B
choices.body: An enterprise VoIP system using encryption

choices.label: D
choices.body: A messaging capability that can function if enterprise authentication is unavailable

stem: Which of the following is not an important part of the incident response communication process?
explanation: Disclosure based on regulatory or legislative requirements is commonly part of an incident response process; however, public feedback is typically a guiding element of information release. Limiting communication to trusted parties and ensuring that data and communications about the incident are properly secured are both critical to the security of the incident response process. This also means that responders should work to limit the potential for accidental release of incident-related information.

choices.label: C
choices.body: Using a secure method of communication

choices.label: D
choices.body: Preventing accidental release of incident-related information

stem: After law enforcement was called because of potential criminal activity discovered as part of a forensic investigation at Joe’s company, the officers on the scene seized three servers. When can Joe expect his servers to be returned?
explanation: Criminal investigations can take very long periods of time to resolve. In most cases, Joe should ensure that he can continue to operate without the servers for the foreseeable future.

choices.label: A
choices.body: After 30 days, which provides enough time for a reasonable imaging process

choices.label: B
choices.body: After 6 months, as required by law

choices.label: C
choices.body: After 1 year, as most cases resolve in that amount of time

choices.label: D
choices.body: Joe should not plan on a time frame for return

stem: Chuck’s organization has prepared draft customer communications as part of their incident response plan. Why is this considered a useful practice?
explanation: Having prewritten communications prepared in case of incidents helps organizations to speed up their communication process. Malicious actors typically don’t target this type of customer communications, and pre-drafting them might allow attackers to modify the drafts. Drafting communications or building templates that include compliance requirements can help make sure compliance requirements are met, but simply drafting them ahead of time does not ensure compliance. The decision to engage law enforcement is not driven by communications.

choices.label: A
choices.body: It prevents malicious actors from changing customer communications.

choices.label: B
choices.body: It ensures compliance requirements are met.

choices.label: C
choices.body: It speeds up communications in many cases.

choices.label: D
choices.body: It avoids the need to engage police.

stem: Ben works at an organization that is required under U.S. law to report HIPAA breaches. Which of the following is not a typical requirement of this type of notification requirement?
explanation: While reporting requirements vary, notifying impacted individuals and the reporting agency are common requirements. HIPAA also requires notification of the media under some circumstances, but does not require notifying law enforcement. If you’re faced with a question like this and aren’t familiar with the specific compliance requirement it can help to consider why the requirement might exist. Here it is to ensure that impacted individuals are more likely to be aware of the breach, and HIPAA requires it if more than 500 residents of a state or jurisdiction are impacted.

stem: Which of the following organizations is not typically involved in post-incident communications?
explanation: Post-incident communication often involves marketing and public relations staff who focus on consumer sentiment and improving the organization’s image, whereas legal often reviews statements to limit liability or other issues. Developers are typically not directly involved in post-incident communications and are instead working on ensuring the security of the applications or systems they are responsible for.

stem: Tom is building his incident response team and is concerned about how the organization will address insider threats. Which business function would be most capable of assisting with the development of disciplinary policies?
explanation: Although all of these functions are likely able to provide important advice on disciplinary policies, the human resources team has primary responsibility for employee relations and would be the best team to include for this purpose.

stem: Craig is revising his organization’s incident response plan and wants to ensure that the plan includes coordination with all relevant internal and external entities. Which one of the following stakeholders should he be most cautious about coordinating with?
explanation: All of these stakeholders should be included in the planning for an incident response program. However, Craig should be most careful about coordinating with external entities, such as regulatory bodies, because of their enforcement role. He should plan to coordinate more freely with internal entities, such as senior leadership, legal, and human resources.

stem: The vulnerability management action plan that was sent to Jacinda notes that a critical application that her organization uses relies on an insecure version of a software package because of a long-standing workflow requirement. Jacinda’s organization’s best practices state that the organization will select the most secure option that also permits business to be conducted. What should Jacinda do?
explanation: Jacinda knows that reviewing business processes to see if they can be changed to use a secure version of the software package may require some business process changes but is often a possible solution. Ignoring the vulnerability isn’t secure, turning off the service will disrupt the business itself, and third-party patches rarely exist and are seldom a preferred solution.

choices.label: B
choices.body: Change the business requirements to enable the vulnerability to be handled.

choices.label: D
choices.body: Install a third-party patch for the service.

stem: What section of an incident response report provides a brief, clear summary of the incident, response activities, and current state of the incident?
explanation: Executive summaries are brief, clear, and focused on conveying the important elements of the IR report. They are typically found at the beginning of the report and are intended to allow leaders and others who read the report to quickly grasp and understand the content of the report.

stem: Ian wants to prepare his organization for communications with the media as part of incident related public relations. What should he recommend that his organization do to prepare?
explanation: Ian knows that media training is a common preparedness item for organizations that may have to respond to the media in the event of an incident. Building a list of phrases and topics to avoid is difficult before an incident and can be problematic if it becomes public. Engaging either legal counsel or a reputation defense firm does not prepare the organization itself for engaging with the media but may be part of post or during the incident activities if the organization feels it to be necessary.

choices.label: A
choices.body: Build a list of phrases and topics to avoid.

stem: Jason is required to notify the company that provides credit card processing services to his organization if an incident impacting credit card data occurs. What type of communications does he need to perform?
explanation: Payment card industry requirements contractual, not regulatory. Jason’s organization is the customer, and law enforcement communication is not required by PCI.

stem: The incident response report that Kathleen has prepared includes the following statement: “Unnecessary services including HTTP and FTP should be disabled on all devices of this type that are deployed.” What incident response reporting component will most commonly include this type of statement?
explanation: The recommendations section of an incident response report will have specific suggestions for changes that will help prevent or limit the impact of future incidents. This statement provides more detail than would typically be found in an executive summary. Timelines specify when something happened but don’t make recommendations, and scope detail provides information about the scale and impacted systems or services from an incident.

stem: What common score is used to help with prioritization of vulnerability remediation in many organizations?
explanation: The Common Vulnerability Scoring System (CVSS) score provides a numerical score that reflects the severity of a vulnerability and is thus useful for prioritization. Common vulnerabilities and exposures (CVE) provides a way to identify and catalog vulnerabilities. ATT&CK is a framework used to define adversarial tactics and techniques, and PASTA is a threat modeling process.

stem: Olivia has been notified that a vulnerability has recurred on a server after being marked as remediated through a compensating control by an administrator. Which of the following is the most likely reason that a vulnerability may recur in this circumstance?
explanation: A common scenario for compensating controls and work-arounds is that a follow-up patch causes the fix to no longer work. This may be because settings are changed or because the service or system has been modified in ways the compensating control did not anticipate. It is less likely that an attacker would remove a patch, or that the system would be reinstalled without reapplying the remediation, and in most environments, users should not be able to change server configurations.

choices.label: A
choices.body: An attacker has removed the patch to expose the vulnerability.

choices.label: B
choices.body: The system has been reinstalled by the administrator.

choices.label: C
choices.body: A patch has caused the compensating control to fail.

choices.label: D
choices.body: The service has been reenabled by a user.

stem: The incident response report that Brian is reading includes a statement that says, “Impacted systems were limited to those in the organization’s AWS VPC.” What part of an incident response report will typically contain this type of information?
explanation: Scope statements are used to explain and define which systems, services, or infrastructure components were part of an incident. Timelines are used to show when events occurred in relation to each other. Evidence is provided as part of a report to show what was found and how it was interpreted. Impact statements describe what the incident’s results or outcomes were for the organization.

stem: Nila’s incident response team has discovered evidence of an employee who may have been engaged in criminal activity while they were conducting an incident investigation. The team has suggested that law enforcement should be contacted. What significant concern should Nila raise about this potential communication?
explanation: Since the violation is only an organizational policy, Nila should note that law enforcement engagement may hinder the organization’s ability to respond or operate. Law enforcement isn’t being asked to enforce organizational policy, the more pressing issue is interruption of business instead of communications issues, and if the employee violated the law an arrest may happen anyway.

choices.label: A
choices.body: Law enforcement can’t enforce organizational policy.

choices.label: B
choices.body: Law enforcement engagement may hinder the organization’s ability to respond or operate.

choices.label: C
choices.body: Law enforcement involvement may create communications issues.

choices.label: D
choices.body: Law enforcement may arrest a critical employee.

stem: Sameer wants to establish and track a metric for his organization that will help him know if his IoC monitoring processes are working well. Which of the following metrics is best suited to determining if IoCs are being effectively captured and analyzed?
explanation: Sameer knows that mean time to detect should be lower if IoCs are being effectively captured, correlated, and analyzed. Mean time to respond measures the time from detection to assessing the event as an incident and activating the process. Mean time to remediate is a much more complex measure to provide a metric for since each incident’s size, scope, and complexity will all influence the mean time to remediate. This metric requires more nuanced communication and explanation than a simple number on a report in many cases and may benefit from granular reporting describing types of incidents as well as their impact and scope. Mean time to compromise is not a metric defenders will typically track.

stem: Sameer is continuing to improve his metrics to report to his organization’s board of directors. The board has requested that he include alert volumes in his reporting. What issue should Sameer discuss with the board after receiving this request?
explanation: Alert volume is not an effective security metric because it is highly impacted by tuning as well as external factors like the number of probes and attacks. High-alert volumes don’t indicate a poor incident response process but may indicate poor tuning or a high number of events. Low-alert volumes may similarly indicate poor tuning or events that are not being detected. Correlating the number of patches with alert volume does not produce a useful metric.

choices.label: A
choices.body: High-alert volumes indicate poor incident response processes.

choices.label: B
choices.body: Low-alert volumes indicate effective incident response processes.

choices.label: C
choices.body: Alert volume is not an effective security metric.

choices.label: D
choices.body: Alert volume requires other measures like number of patches installed to be an effective security metric.

stem: What important incident response report section relies heavily on NTP to be successful?
explanation: Network Time Protocol (NTP) is used to synchronize clocks and thus keeps log entries set to the proper time. Without synchronized time between systems, log entries can be extremely difficult to correlate, and timelines are difficult to build properly.

stem: What type of agreement between two organizations is a common inhibitor to remediation because of uptime requirements?
explanation: Service level agreements (SLAs) often have uptime requirements included in their metrics and measures. Since patching may require systems or services to be offline, an SLA is a common inhibitor to remediation. Nondisclosure agreements (NDAs) and key performance indicators (KPIs) are not common inhibitors to remediation, and a TLA is just a “three-letter acronym”!

stem: Valerie needs to explain CVSS score metrics to her team. Which of the following is not part of the basic metric group for CVSS scores?
explanation: The basic metric group for CVSS includes the attack vector, the attack complexity, the privileges required, user interaction, and four impact metrics: compatibility, integrity, availability, and scope. The maturity of exploit code is part of the temporal metric group, not the basic metric group.

choices.label: B
choices.body: The maturity of the exploit code

stem: The scientific instrument that Chas is responsible for has multiple critical severity vulnerabilities in its operating system and services. The device cannot be patched according to instructions from the vendor who provides it. Which of the following is not an appropriate compensating control in this scenario?
explanation: Patching against vendor recommendations is the only control on this list that does not meet business requirements. Using a firewall device, disabling network connectivity, and moving the device to an isolated and secure network segment are all common compensating controls in this type of scenario.

choices.label: A
choices.body: Place a network security device configured to prevent access to the system between the instrument and the network.

choices.label: C
choices.body: Disable network connectivity to the device.

choices.label: D
choices.body: Place the device on a protected network segment.

stem: Hui’s incident response report includes log entries showing that a user logged in from another country, despite living and working in the country that the company Hui works for is located in. What incident response report section is most likely to contain this type of information?
explanation: Log entries showing logins from a country where the employee does not work or reside are an example of evidence that may be included in an incident response report.

stem: Melissa is conducting a root-cause analysis. Which of the following is not a common step in RCA processes?
explanation: The four stages of RCA are identifying problems and events that occurred as part of the incident, establishing a timeline of events, differentiating between the events and causal factors, and documenting the root-cause analysis. Root-cause analyses result in a report, which may then be used as part of preparation processes where compensating controls may be employed. Implementing compensating controls isn’t typically part of the RCA process itself.

choices.label: C
choices.body: Differentiate causal factors and the root cause.

stem: What information is typically included in a list of affected hosts in a vulnerability management report?
explanation: The hostname and IP address are commonly used to identify each vulnerable host in a vulnerability report. The hardware (MAC) address is not typically listed, and subnet masks are also not typically listed.

stem: Hannah wants to establish a metric that will help her organization determine if their response process completes in a timely manner. Which common metric should she select to help assess this?
explanation: Assessing whether incidents are remediated in a timely manner can help Hannah determine if IR completion is happening in a timely manner since remediation is the last nonreporting stage in the process and reporting is not typically a process where time to complete is critical to an organization.

stem: Mikayla’s team has determined that a previously remediated vulnerability has reappeared after installation of a vendor supplied patch. What type of vulnerability management issue is this?
explanation: This is an example of recurrence and is something that should be reported on as part of Mikalya’s ongoing vulnerability reporting and exception management process. No risk scoring or prioritization is mentioned, and while mitigation was performed, reappearing vulnerabilities are recurrence, not mitigation.

stem: Gurvinder wants to consider impact metrics like the integrity impact, availability impact, and compatibility impact of a vulnerability that is scored using CVSS. What metric group includes this information?
explanation: The Basic Metric Group for CVSS includes both exploitability metrics and impact metrics. The impact metric is made up of components covering compatibility, integrity, and availability impact as well as scope.

stem: Which of the following is not a type of stakeholder that will frequently need to understand an organization’s overall vulnerability stance or status?
explanation: The legal team rarely needs to know an organization’s vulnerability management status or stance. Security, audit, and compliance stakeholders do.

stem: Which of the following CVSS scores indicates the highest impact to an organization?
explanation: CVSS scores range from 0 to 10, with higher scores having greater impact, exploitability, temporal, and environmental factors. Without more context, the highest number will generally indicate the highest impact.

stem: Expectations of time to remediate and time to patch by a vendor are both examples of what in a vulnerability management program?
explanation: Service level objectives (SLOs) are part of a service level agreement (SLA) with a vendor. Time to remediate and time to patch are not risks or vulnerabilities, and internal policies do not determine vendor expectations without a contract or agreement in place.

stem: What issue is organizational governance likely to cause in a vulnerability management program?
explanation: Governance processes are most likely to lead to slower patching processes because of approval requirements. They typically do not prevent patches from being installed or the use of compensating controls, although it may take some time to identify which option will be put in place. It typically doesn’t increase the number of vulnerabilities that need to be patched, nor do they typically limit what vulnerabilities will be patched.

choices.label: A
choices.body: It may prevent vulnerabilities from being patched or compensating controls being used.

choices.label: B
choices.body: It may increase the number of vulnerabilities that need patched.

choices.label: D
choices.body: It may limit the vulnerabilities that will be patched.

stem: Jacob has initiated the incident response process in his organization. IoCs have been identified, and Jacob is ready to take the next step in the process. What typically happens next?
explanation: Just because IoCs exist doesn’t mean that an incident has occurred. Instead, responders need to analyze the data available and to look for additional information that will tell if the incident is a real incident or a false positive. Notifying counsel or law enforcement happens after an incident is verified and only if needed. Collecting forensic data happens once the organization determines that an incident has occurred and wants to investigate it.

choices.label: D
choices.body: Incident responders determine if it is a real incident.

stem: What is the primary difference between mean time to close and mean time to respond?
explanation: Mean time to close measures the entire length of an incident response process from start to final report and closure. Mean time to respond measures how long it takes a team to begin initial response.

choices.label: A
choices.body: Mean time to close measures the entire incident response process; mean time to respond measures how long it takes to begin initial response.

choices.label: B
choices.body: Mean time to close measures how long it takes to stop a specific compromise; mean time to respond measures how long the compromise is active.

choices.label: C
choices.body: Mean time to close and mean time to respond have the same meaning, but are measured from removal of the malware, and discovery of the malware respectively.

choices.label: D
choices.body: Mean time to close measures the time from IoC removal to the final report; mean time to respond measures how long it takes to begin initial response.

stem: Melissa’s organization relies on a file sharing function built into their business software. A recent security flaw has resulted in the next patch removing the file sharing functionality. Melissa’s team has been asked by the functional offices who use the tool to delay the patch to allow them to identify a work-around. What inhibitor to remediation has Melissa encountered?
explanation: Melissa’s team is working to counter issues with degrading functionality. If the patch is installed, critical business processes will be disrupted. No mention is made of contractual agreements or governance that will be impacted, and the software is not described as a legacy system. Instead, it is receiving patches and updates.

stem: Which of the following is the best indicator of a successful security awareness effort?
explanation: Phishing campaign click rates can help you determine if your awareness efforts are successful. Low rates are typically indicative of successful awareness efforts. False positive and true positive rates are more typically associated with work from the security team to decrease incorrect identification, and mean time to respond is improved through process improvements.

stem: Annie’s organization makes divisional administrators responsible for patching vulnerabilities after they are notified of them using a ticketing system. Annie has noticed that the administrators are not promptly patching systems. What should she do to most effectively address this issue?
explanation: Awareness and training programs are an important part of vulnerability management practices, and Annie can expect that if administrators understand their roles, job requirements, and the importance of patching that they will more promptly patch systems they are responsible for. Switching notification styles is unlikely to have a major impact, attacking systems is not a common or typically acceptable practice in most organizations, and escalating to HR may lead to resentment and shouldn’t be Annie’s first option.

choices.label: B
choices.body: Invest in an awareness and training campaign.

choices.label: C
choices.body: Use the vulnerabilities to compromise the systems to prove a point.

choices.label: D
choices.body: Involve HR due to a lack of job performance.

stem: Henry’s organization handles credit card data as part of their operations. What type of vulnerability management report is Henry most likely to need to run due to this?
explanation: Henry’s organization is most likely to need to be compliant with the Payment Card Industry (PCI) standards and thus will need to run reports that will help prove PCI compliance. A list of compromised or unpatched systems is not required for PCI.

stem: Jen has discovered that many systems in her organization are being deployed with a vulnerable service active. What solution is best suited to addressing this type of issue in a large organization?
explanation: Jen knows that configuration management is an appropriate solution to ensure that organization wide standards are met and that it can help with this type of issue. She may also need to implement an awareness program to ensure that admins are appropriately configuring systems before deployment, but configuration management is the more complete fix. Compensating controls aren’t indicated by the question, and changing business requirements isn’t a demonstrated need either.

stem: An incident report should indicate the individuals involved, as well as which of the following items?
explanation: Incident reports typically need to include who, what, when, where, and why. Hardware addresses, written statements from those involved, and police reports are rarely included.

choices.label: A
choices.body: The hardware addresses of the systems involved

choices.label: B
choices.body: The time frame the event or incident occurred

choices.label: C
choices.body: A written statement from each individual interviewed

stem: Jason has defined the problem as part of a root-cause analysis effort. What step typically comes next in RCA?
explanation: Root-cause analysis requires data to proceed, and Jason knows that his next step is to collect data. Then he will proceed to determining causal factors, identifying the root cause, and prioritizing causes.

choices.label: B
choices.body: Determining the root cause of the problem

stem: Mean time to respond is an example of what?
explanation: Mean time to respond is a key performance indicator (KPI) for incident response.

stem: What information is gathered as part of a lessons learned exercise conducted at the end of an incident response process?
explanation: Lessons learned should include both positive and negative lessons learned. This ensures that organizations reinforce what goes well and improve what goes badly. Root causes are identified as part of a root-cause analysis, not as part of lessons learned.

choices.label: A
choices.body: Issues that will positively impact future incident response processes

choices.label: B
choices.body: Both positive and negative lessons learned during the process

choices.label: C
choices.body: Issues that will negatively impact future incident response processes

stem: Jason wants to quickly understand the content of an incident report. What should he read?
explanation: Executive summaries should be short and to the point and are intended to allow readers to quickly understand the content of the report without reading the full report. Scope statements describe the scale and impacted systems or services, timelines list when events happened, and evidence provides detailed information about the incident that support analysis or theories.

stem: What important role does criticality and impact information play in organizational use of CVSS scores?
explanation: Combining criticality and impact information organizations can determine both how dangerous the issue is and how likely it is to impact them. That means that CVSS can provide a useful rating to prioritize their efforts given limited resources and time. Recurrence is not impacted by criticality or impact, and instead tends to point to technical or procedural issues. Compensating controls are used when a patch is not available or the fix does not meet the business needs of an organization. Patch installation is determined by administrators based on testing and organizational policies which may be influenced by criticality and impact for prioritization.

choices.label: B
choices.body: It determines if a patch should be installed.

choices.label: C
choices.body: It determines if a compensating control should be used.

stem: Natalie has signed a service level agreement with a customer that specifies performance requirements for a service that her company provides. How is this most likely to impact her ability to remediate vulnerabilities on the underlying containerized services that provide the service?
explanation: The fact that Natalie’s organization uses containers will likely help her to avoid unexpected or unwanted downtime, but Natalie still needs to ensure the service is not interrupted as she deployed patched containers and removes the old vulnerable containers. An SLA does not require external governance; instead, it determines key aspects of the performance of the service like uptime, and downtime is rarely unlimited. Otherwise, an SLA wouldn’t be in use. Finally, there is no mention of legacy systems in this question.

choices.label: A
choices.body: It will require Natalie to seek customer approval for each patch that is deployed via their governance process.

choices.label: B
choices.body: It will require Natalie to ensure that the service is not disrupted when new, patched containers are deployed and vulnerable containers are disabled.

choices.label: C
choices.body: It will allow as much downtime as needed as patches are deployed to the containerized services.

choices.label: D
choices.body: It will prevent Natalie from upgrading the legacy systems the customer relies on.

stem: Angela’s organization has discovered that their Windows workstations have a vulnerability that was discovered more than a year ago. What solution is best suited to handling this known vulnerability?
explanation: Angela knows that simply patching it is likely the best option. A well-known Windows vulnerability will typically have an available patch. She should find out why her organization has failed to patch it and address the issue. That may require awareness or training once she figures out why the patching isn’t happening! Compensating controls are typically not necessary for an older, known vulnerability in a supported product because patches usually exist, and there’s no indication in the question of a business process change that would help.

stem: Jacob notes that the patch for a critical flaw requires a service to be disabled. He knows that the service provides backend connectivity for a tool that his sales teams use, and that they will need to use email to communicate about sales once the patch is installed. What type of remediation issue is this?
explanation: This is an issue with degrading functionality. Organizations may have to choose between retaining functionality and installing patches, and Jacob will have to work with business functional leaders to determine the impact of the patch versus the risk of a compensating control or simply not installing the patch. The patch is available, so it’s not an issue of patch availability—although sometimes the patch that is available may not be the final patch that allows functionality to work. Proprietary data is not a typical inhibitor of remediation, and there is no indication this is a legacy system.

stem: Bob is a security analyst responsible for vulnerability scanning and reporting in his organization. He has noticed a trend of unpatched vulnerabilities on systems that process data covered by PCI-DSS. What should he note to management?
explanation: PCI-DSS is the payment card industry’s standard for security, and unpatched vulnerabilities on systems that need to be PCI-DSS compliant makes this a compliance issue. There’s not enough detail to determine why patches aren’t installed, encryption is not indicated by the question, and there is no information that should cause you to think that these are proprietary systems.

choices.label: A
choices.body: The systems have a compliance issue.

choices.label: B
choices.body: The patches are not installing properly due to misconfiguration.

choices.label: C
choices.body: Encryption is causing problems with patching.

choices.label: D
choices.body: The systems are proprietary and patches may not be available.

stem: Gurvinder’s organization is required to report breaches within 24 hours of the breach being detected, regardless of how far into the investigation the organization is. What type of requirement is most likely to drive this type of communication?
explanation: Regulatory requirements often have specific time frames for communication, regardless of the state of the incident response process. Contractual requirements tend to offer the organization more flexibility in reporting. Social media does not create requirements, and reputation may benefit from timely notification but does not result in requirements either.

stem: Xuan’s organization uses an old, no longer updated or sold software package that has an embedded web server that it exposes on every workstation that runs the software allowing file transfer between workstations. During a vulnerability scan the web browser was highlighted as a critical vulnerability. Which of the following solutions should Xuan recommend to best resolve the issue?
explanation: Xuan should recommend that the organization change business practices. There are many other ways to exchange files that do not require a vulnerable software package, and change in process would resolve this. Awareness, compensating controls, and configuration management do not address the business need.

stem: Jackie is reviewing the risk scores round in a vulnerability report and notes that the risk she is reviewing scores a 1.0. What recommendation should Jackie make about the vulnerability?
explanation: While a risk as low as 1.0 on the CVSS scale is unlikely to cause immediate harm, if a patch is available and does not introduce additional risk, it should still be installed at the next patch window.

choices.label: A
choices.body: It should be patched immediately because the risk score is high.

choices.label: B
choices.body: The risk is very low and can likely be ignored.

choices.label: C
choices.body: The risk is low and should be patched in the next patch cycle.

choices.label: D
choices.body: It should be patched immediately because it is in the top 10 percent of risks.

stem: Log entries are commonly found in what part of an incident response report?
explanation: The evidence section of an incident response report often includes information like log entries. Log files typically don’t show up in the executive summary, the timeline, or the recommendations section of the report.

stem: Kathleen wants to build a prioritized list of vulnerabilities for her organization. What part of the CVSS metric will help her adjust the score to best match her organization’s availability requirements?
explanation: The environmental group includes information that takes an organization’s specific requirements into account including availability requirements the organization itself establishes. Even if you’re not familiar with the CVSS scoring system’s three groupings (basic, temporal, and environmental), you can likely answer a question like this by considering the likely meaning of each of these options.

stem: Derek is the lead of his organization’s finance and accounting team and has expressed concerns about installing patches because his team relies on the service that is being patched. Derek noted that the team is at a critical time because of annual financial reports. What type of inhibitor to remediation is this?
explanation: This is an example of a business process interruption issue. Organizations are often sensitive to downtime and outages that could be caused by patching and vulnerability remediation during sensitive or busy parts of their business cycle. This often drives “freezes” or other windows where patching may be paused or delayed. There is no mention of a MOU or SLA that would be breached, and the system is not described as being a legacy system, making these less likely choices.

stem: What part of an incident response report describes detailed ways to avoid similar issues in the future?
explanation: Incident response reports should include a lessons learned listing that describes ways to improve as well as how to avoid similar issues in the future. The executive summary is brief, and while it may point to lessons learned, it will not typically cover them in depth. The scope statement for an incident describes what systems, services, or other elements and assets of the organizations were impacted. Evidence provides information about how the incident was detected.

stem: Potential compensating controls can be found in what section of a vulnerability management report?
explanation: Compensating controls are an example of a mitigation technique and can be found as part of the mitigation recommendations.

stem: The company that Amari works for uses an embedded system as part of a manufacturing process. The system relies on an operating system created by the machine’s vendor, and Amari’s team has identified vulnerabilities during a network scan. What type of system should Amari identify this device as?
explanation: This is an example of a proprietary system that may not use commonly available and supported operating systems or software. Legacy systems are out-of-date, often unsupported systems. Primary and secondary systems are not terms typically used to categorize vulnerable systems.

stem: Amari has discovered that a phishing email campaign has been successful and that multiple accounts have been accessed by malicious actors. What should she do next?
explanation: Amari’s first priority should be declaring an incident. Once an incident has been declared, she can take further action while following her organization’s incident response process, which may include actions like creating an IoC, guidance on when and why to contact law enforcement, or taking actions like blacklisting senders.

choices.label: C
choices.body: Mark the sender in her organization’s phishing blacklist.

choices.label: D
choices.body: Create an IoC based on the phishing email.

stem: Amari has deployed a compensating control to protect the vulnerable embedded system that she is responsible for. What step should she take next?
explanation: Amari should note the compensating control and ensure that periodic review is done to determine if new patches are required or any additional compensating controls or maintenance of the firewall device is required. No incident occurred, meaning an incident report is not necessary. The device should not be removed from the vulnerability scanning system because it remains on the network. The vulnerabilities were not false positives and should not be treated as such.

choices.label: A
choices.body: Create an incident report and distribute it to appropriate recipients.

choices.label: B
choices.body: Remove the device from the vulnerability scanning process to avoid continued false positives.

choices.label: C
choices.body: Note the compensating control and flag the device for follow-up to see if patches become available.

choices.label: D
choices.body: Flag the vulnerabilities previously discovered as false positives.

stem: As part of their contracted support model, Christina’s organization ensures that patches are installed within 14 calendar days, and that critical patches are installed within 48 hours of their release. What term best describes this type of agreement?
explanation: This is an example of a service level agreement, or SLA. Christina’s organization has set a performance level that they will meet and can be assessed against. If they fail, contractual penalties may apply. An NDA is a nondisclosure agreement, used to protect confidential information. Organizational governance reviews and approves changes and other actions, and might be involved in setting or agreeing to SLAs, and a KPI is a key performance indicator. If the question asked about the organization measuring how often they achieve the stated numbers, that would be an example of a KPI.

stem: Michele’s root-cause analysis has determined a number of events that contributed to the problem but were not the root cause. What has she identified?
explanation: Causal factors are events that contribute to an incident but that are not the root cause.

stem: What three groups of metrics make up a CVSS score?
explanation: CVSS scores are based on three sets of metrics: the Base, Temporal, and Environmental groups.

choices.label: A
choices.body: The Core Metric Group, the Impact Metric Group, and the Organizational Metric Group

choices.label: B
choices.body: The Core Metric Group, the Temporal Metric Group, and the Organizational Metric Group

choices.label: C
choices.body: The Basic Metric Group, the Impact Metric Group, and the Environmental Metric Group

choices.label: D
choices.body: The Basic Metric Group, the Temporal Metric Group, and the Environmental Metric Group

stem: Which of the following questions is not typically answered as part of an incident response report?
explanation: It may seem like common sense, but answering the five Ws (who, what, when, where, and why) is common in incident response reports. With whom, however, is not one of the five Ws.

stem: Michelle has been working to contain an incident for the past eight hours and her shift is ending. Which of the following is the most important to include in her shift handoff documentation to ensure that the incident response process continues successfully?
explanation: During an active incident the most important information on this list is knowing the containment status. Since the problem doesn’t note that Michelle has successfully contained the issue, handing that task off is critical. IoCs may be useful as part of the response, but without knowing where she left off, the next shift would be starting from an unknown state. Root-cause analysis happens after an incident, not during, and a communications plan might be useful but isn’t as critical as the status information until the issue is contained.

choices.label: B
choices.body: The status of the containment effort

choices.label: D
choices.body: A media communications plan with next steps included

stem: Which of the following is most important when tailoring a threat intelligence report for an organization?
explanation: Understanding the organization’s critical asset inventory allows security analysts to tailor threat intelligence reports to focus on threats to the organization. The type of security devices is part of security design, but doesn’t impact threat intelligence reporting as much as a complete list of critical assets which may include many of those devices. Major incident information should influence security plans and may guide some threat intelligence reporting but understanding the organization’s critical assets is more important when considering what threats to pay attention to. Finally, cyber insurance thresholds are critical for incident response practices and as part of risk management, but aren’t used for tailoring threat intelligence reports.

choices.label: A
choices.body: The number and type of security devices deployed by the organization

choices.label: C
choices.body: A list of major incidents from the last three years

stem: The trend for Katie’s vulnerability remediation time to resolve has been decreasing for the past six months. What should Katie do?
explanation: A decreasing trend in time to remediate is a desirable outcome. Katie should continue what her organization is doing, or could potentially choose to do more of whatever is causing the trend to improve! None of the other response choices are required when a trend is moving in a positive direction.

choices.label: A
choices.body: Modify the vulnerability scanning process to better detect new vulnerabilities.

choices.label: B
choices.body: Continue operations; this is a desired result.

choices.label: C
choices.body: Invest more resources to increase the time to remediate instead.

choices.label: D
choices.body: Investigate false positive rates to improve remediation.

stem: Josh’s organization is preparing to install a series of critical patches when a departmental business manager refuses to sign off on the patch. After discussing the issue with the manager, Josh is informed that the patch documentation notes that a function that that manager’s team uses frequently will be disabled by the patch. How should Josh categorize this issue?
explanation: This is an example of degraded functionality. The department may need the functionality to perform business functions, and organizational governance may now have to decide if the business team needs to find another way to accomplish the task or if a compensating control may be appropriate. There is nothing to indicate that this is a legacy or proprietary system, and there is no mention of a contractual requirement for this functionality.

choices.label: C
choices.body: A problem due to a contractual agreement

stem: Oliver’s team has updated their risk scorecard, and has discovered that the organization’s risk posture has gotten worse due to more unpatched critical vulnerabilities. What recommendation should he make to best address this concern?
explanation: Reviewing the organization’s patching practices to identify any issues that are delaying or impacting remediation and taking action to improve time to patch Oliver’s team should decrease the number of unpatched critical vulnerabilities. In most organizations host firewalls should already be in place, meaning that exposed services will remain open and patches remain important. Removing unpatched systems from the network will impact functionality and will likely have business impacts, and asking for more budget in an annual cycle doesn’t not have a timely impact.

choices.label: A
choices.body: Review patching practices and take action to improve time to patch.

choices.label: B
choices.body: Install host firewalls to better protect the open services while they are waiting to be patched.

choices.label: C
choices.body: Remove unpatched systems from the network until they can be patched.

choices.label: D
choices.body: Ask for more budget for security operations in the next annual budget cycle.

stem: After a recent critical update Jill has noticed that her organization’s vulnerability scans are returning many critical findings across many Windows 11 workstations that upon further investigation are false positives. What issue is most likely occurring?
explanation: The most likely answer is that the scanner’s definitions for the vulnerability are not properly recognizing the patch. Examples of this occur when a detection focuses on a version number or other identifier that is not updated despite the underlying vulnerability being fixed. Scanning the wrong systems across a large number of workstations is unlikely, rebooting will typically enable patches, not disable them, and host firewalls will typically block scans, not cause a false positive identification of a vulnerability.

choices.label: A
choices.body: The vulnerability scanner is scanning the wrong systems.

choices.label: B
choices.body: Patches were installed but the scanner is not detecting them properly.

choices.label: C
choices.body: Patches were installed before the systems were rebooted.

choices.label: D
choices.body: The systems have host firewalls enabled.

stem: After remediating her organization’s false positive rates for scans, Jill focuses on ensuring that identification of vulnerabilities accurately reflects the status of her systems. What is this called?
explanation: True positive rates measure actual detections. Here Jill has worked to ensure that her detections are real, lowering her false positive rate and increasing her true positive rate. Adjusted rate and vulnerability rate were made up for this question.

stem: Jason’s organization wants to align their security program with their risks. What two factors should they assess to ensure their top risks match the business’s needs?
explanation: Jason knows that assessing threats and their potential impacts specific to his organization will result in the most accurate top risks list for his organization. Industrywide data, regardless of whether it’s through SANS, publicly reported incidents, or IoCs associated with the industry as a whole, will be less directly relevant.

choices.label: A
choices.body: Assess IoCs for their industry and compare it to industry numbers for impact.

choices.label: B
choices.body: Assess threats specific to their company and the impact of their occurrence.

choices.label: C
choices.body: Leverage the SANS Top 10 and combine it with their own risk assessment.

choices.label: D
choices.body: Review recent incidents nationwide and their impacts based on actual events that have been publicly reported.

stem: Geoff has been notified that his Windows 10 system is out of main-line support and is no longer supported by his organization’s patching processes and desktop support team. He needs the system to continue running, as the software it runs is highly specialized and is not compatible with Windows 11. What type of inhibitor to remediation is this?
explanation: This is an example of a legacy system. While Windows 10 only recently went out of mainstream support, the lack of patch availability and support from his organization makes this a legacy system issue. There’s no contractual agreement, and functionality is not being degraded. While there are workarounds from Microsoft for some Windows 10 systems, this isn’t a governance issue, as the system is now a legacy system.

stem: Val is responsible for security for an organization that runs numerous scientific devices. Among them are specialized sensors that are network connected, but that do not run commodity operating systems. What type of inhibitor to remediation should she identify this as?
explanation: These are proprietary systems. Nothing is noted about issues with patch availability, although patch availability is also more common with proprietary systems. No performance issues are indicated, and these are not described as being legacy systems.

stem: Frankie has reviewed her organization’s mean time to close statistics and believes that process improvement is needed. Which of the following is most likely to positively impact mean time to close?
explanation: Decreasing the time it takes to respond to an incident will impact how quickly they are dealt with and will result in a shorter time to close. Decreasing alert volume may help, but there isn’t enough information to determine if this is a driver of slowdowns. Increasing mean time to detect makes things slower, and increasing a false positive rate means the organization will spend more time chasing down incorrectly identified issues.

choices.label: B
choices.body: Decreasing her organization’s mean time to respond

choices.label: C
choices.body: Increasing her team’s mean time to detect

choices.label: D
choices.body: Increasing her organization’s false positive rate

stem: Klara’s team wants to establish a metric that will help determine if their incident response process is working well. Which of the following metrics should they monitor to determine if the process of moving from detecting an IoC to investigating it as a potential incident is working well?
explanation: The mean time to respond for an organization is determined by how long on average it takes the organization to identify and respond to an incident. This is a useful way to look at whether the move from detection to investigation is working well. Alert volume helps to measure if tuning is being done appropriately, mean time to close measures how long it takes organizations to fully resolve incidents, and false positive rates measure when detections are wrong.

stem: Hung wants to tailor a threat intelligence summary about a new phishing campaign for his organization’s SOC. Which of the following best describes the tailoring he should perform?
explanation: A SOC will be concerned with detecting and potentially stopping the phishing attack meaning that IoCs are the most valuable things that Hung can provide them with. Forensic artifacts and malware payload information will be useful to incident response staff, business risks and strategy are appropriate for management, and remediation plans for desktops and other devices may be used by technical support staff or for incident responders.

choices.label: A
choices.body: It should include IoCs related to the phishing attack and to the suspected threat actor.

choices.label: B
choices.body: It should focus on forensic artifacts and should include details of the malware payloads delivered to victims.

choices.label: C
choices.body: It should focus on business risk and strategic implications of the phishing attack if successful.

choices.label: D
choices.body: It should include remediation plans for impacted desktops and other devices.

stem: While reviewing network flow logs, John sees that network flow on a particular segment suddenly dropped to zero. What is the most likely cause of this?
explanation: The sudden drop to zero is most likely to be an example of link failure. A denial-of-service attack could result in this type of drop but is less likely for most organizations. High bandwidth consumption and beaconing both have different traffic patterns from the one shown in this example.

stem: Saanvi is conducting the recovery process after his organization experienced a security incident. During that process, he plans to apply patches to all of the systems in his environment. Which one of the following should be his highest priority for patching?
explanation: During an incident recovery effort, patching priority should be placed on systems that were directly involved in the incident. This is one component of remediating known issues that were actively exploited.

stem: Susan’s organization suffered a major breach attributed to an advanced persistent threat (APT) that exploited zero-day vulnerabilities to gain control of systems on her company’s network. She is evaluating different defensive approaches with her security team. Which of the following is the least appropriate solution for Susan to recommend to help prevent future attacks of this type?
explanation: Signature-based attack detection methods rely on knowing what an attack or malware looks like. Zero-day attacks are unlikely to have an existing signature, making signature-based detection ineffective against them. Heuristic (behavior) detection methods can indicate compromises despite the lack of signatures for the specific exploit. Building a well-designed and segmented network can limit the impact of compromises or even prevent them. Leveraging threat intelligence to understand new attacks and countermeasures is an important part of defense against zero-day attacks.

stem: During his investigation of a Windows system, Eric discovered that files were deleted and he wants to determine whether a specific file previously existed on the computer. Which of the following is the least likely to be a potential location to discover evidence supporting that theory?
explanation: The Windows Registry, Master File Tables, and INDX records all contain information about files, often including removed or deleted files. Event logs are far less likely to contain information about a specific file location.

stem: As part of her SOC analyst duties, Emily is tasked with monitoring intrusion detection systems that cover her employer’s corporate headquarters network. During her shift, Emily’s IDS alarms report that a network scan has occurred from a system with IP address 10.0.11.19 on the organization’s WPA3 Enterprise wireless network aimed at systems in the finance division. What data source should she check first?
explanation: Since Emily’s organization uses WPA3 Enterprise, users must authenticate to use the wireless network. Associating the scan with an authenticated user will help incident responders identify the device that conducted the scan. Therefore, Emily should first check wireless authentication logs.

stem: Casey’s incident response process leads her to a production server that must stay online for her company’s business to remain operational. What method should she use to capture the data she needs?
explanation: Normally, forensic images are collected from systems that are offline to ensure that a complete copy is made. In cases like this where keeping the system online is more important than the completeness of the forensic image, a live image to an external drive using a portable forensic tool such as FTK Imager Lite, the dd command-line utility, or similar is the correct choice.

choices.label: A
choices.body: Live image to an external drive.

choices.label: B
choices.body: Live image to the system’s primary drive.

choices.label: C
choices.body: Take the system offline and image to an external drive.

choices.label: D
choices.body: Take the system offline, install a write blocker on the system’s primary drive, and then image it to an external drive.

stem: What does the Nmap response “filtered” mean in port scan results?
